// Article-specific bespoke detection — DynoWiper update: Technical analysis and attribution
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("schtask.exe", "schtask2.exe", "_update.exe", "rubeus.exe", "tmp_backup.tmp.exe", "ts_5wb.tmp.exe", "rsocx.exe") or FolderPath has_any ("C:\inetpub\pub\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("C:\inetpub\pub\") or FileName in~ ("schtask.exe", "schtask2.exe", "_update.exe", "rubeus.exe", "tmp_backup.tmp.exe", "ts_5wb.tmp.exe", "rsocx.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

``` Article-specific bespoke detection — DynoWiper update: Technical analysis and attribution ```

]

3541.def:
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Gone Phishin': npm Packages Serving Custom Credential Harvesting Pages
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("min.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("min.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
3541.spl:
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — Gone Phishin': npm Packages Serving Custom Credential Harvesting Pages ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("min.js"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("min.js"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

3618.def:
// RomCom CVE-2025-8088 stage-2 — signed Python launched from a transient path so the
// adversary's adjacent malicious python3xx.dll satisfies the import search order.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "python.exe"
      or FileName =~ "pythonw.exe"
      or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^python3\d{1,2}\.exe$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
// suppress the rare legit case of a Python installer extracting itself
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          PythonImage = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
          ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc

// s1ngularity: AI CLI launched with safety-bypass flags as part of credential recon

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("claude","gemini","q")
   or FolderPath endswith "/claude" or FolderPath endswith "/gemini" or FolderPath endswith "/q"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dangerously-skip-permissions","--yolo","--trust-all-tools")

          HasInventoryPrompt, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("prebid.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,

3673.def:
// Linux-only — /proc is a Linux concept. Restrict to Linux endpoints (CI runners, build agents).
let _linux_hosts = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | where OSPlatform == "Linux"
    | summarize by DeviceId;
let _debuggers = dynamic(["gdb","lldb","strace","ltrace","perf","systemd-coredump","gcore","valgrind","apport","abrt-hook-ccpp","crash"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (_linux_hosts)
// Article's Python payload: open('/proc/{pid}/maps','r') and open('/proc/{pid}/mem','rb')
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^/proc/\d+/?$"
| where FileName in~ ("mem","maps")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (_debuggers)
// Exclude self-introspection (process reading /proc/self/* — common in libc/golang runtimes)
| extend AccessedPid = extract(@"^/proc/(\d+)", 1, FolderPath)
| where AccessedPid != tostring(InitiatingProcessId)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          FolderPath, FileName, AccessedPid, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
3673.sent:
// Sentinel ASIM file events — covers auditd / Sysmon-for-Linux / MDE-Linux normalised feeds
let _debuggers = dynamic(["gdb","lldb","strace","ltrace","perf","systemd-coredump","gcore","valgrind","apport"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileAccessed","FileOpened","FileRead","FileCreated")
// Article's payload reads /proc/<N>/mem and /proc/<N>/maps
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/proc/\d+/(mem|maps)$"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (_debuggers)
| extend AccessedPid = extract(@"^/proc/(\d+)/", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where AccessedPid != tostring(ActingProcessId)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetFilePath, AccessedPid, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: |
  Detects a non-debugger Linux process opening /proc/<N>/mem or /proc/<N>/maps —
  the exact credential-dump technique used in the AWS CodeBuild July 2025
  incident (CVE-2025-8217) and the tj-actions/changed-files + reviewdog
  supply-chain attacks (CVE-2025-30066). The malicious payload scans
  /proc/*/cmdline for the CI runner process (e.g. 'Runner.Worker') then reads
  its memory regions to extract repository access tokens.

  category: file_access

3690.sent:
// Hunt CVE-2025-29927 exploitation: external clients sending the bypass header to self-hosted Next.js apps.
// Header lives in WAF / reverse-proxy event text. AppServiceHTTPLogs does not surface arbitrary request
// headers, so we cover WAF (CommonSecurityLog) + raw nginx/IIS via Syslog/W3CIISLog where ingested.
let Window = 7d;
// Path 1 — WAF / reverse-proxy events that log full request headers/context
let WafHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where (RequestContext has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (Message has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString1 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString2 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString3 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString4 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString5 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString6 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct,
              DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication,
              Evidence = coalesce(RequestContext, Message, DeviceCustomString1, DeviceCustomString2, DeviceCustomString3, DeviceCustomString4, DeviceCustomString5, DeviceCustomString6),
              Layer = "WAF";
// Path 2 — raw nginx / Apache access logs forwarded via Syslog (some teams strip headers, some don't)
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where SyslogMessage has "x-middleware-subrequest"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = HostIP, SourceUserName = "", DeviceVendor = "linux", DeviceProduct = Facility,
              DestinationHostName = HostName, RequestURL = "", RequestMethod = "", RequestClientApplication = "",
              Evidence = SyslogMessage, Layer = "Syslog";
// Path 3 — IIS reverse-proxy in front of Next.js (header value sometimes ends up in csUriQuery via URL Rewrite Module)
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where csUriQuery has "x-middleware-subrequest" or csReferer has "x-middleware-subrequest"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, SourceUserName = csUserName, DeviceVendor = "iis", DeviceProduct = "W3CIISLog",
              DestinationHostName = Computer, RequestURL = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), RequestMethod = csMethod,
              RequestClientApplication = csUserAgent,
              Evidence = strcat(csUriQuery, " | ", csReferer), Layer = "IIS";
union isfuzzy=true WafHits, SyslogHits, IISHits
| extend SourceIP = tostring(SourceIP)
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleEvidence = any(Evidence), Hosts = make_set(DestinationHostName, 25),
            URLs = make_set(RequestURL, 25), UAs = make_set(RequestClientApplication, 10),
            Layers = make_set(Layer, 5)
    by SourceIP
| order by FirstSeen asc

status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP requests carrying the x-middleware-subrequest header used to bypass Next.js middleware authorization (CVE-2025-29927). This header is internal-only and should never be present on traffic from external clients.
references:

  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1556
  - cve.2025.29927
logsource:
  category: webserver

  selection_header:
    cs-headers|contains: 'x-middleware-subrequest'
  selection_alt:
    - http_request_headers|contains: 'x-middleware-subrequest'

status: experimental
description: Detects the OpenSSH daemon loading the malicious liblzma.so.5.6.0 or liblzma.so.5.6.1 introduced by the xz-utils supply chain backdoor (CVE-2024-3094). The backdoor activates when sshd, via libsystemd notification patches, chain-loads the compromised liblzma — at which point the IFUNC crc64_resolve audit hook hijacks RSA_public_decrypt and enables authentication bypass for a holder of the attacker's RSA key.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/the-xz-backdoor-cve-2024-3094/
  - https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2024-3094-detecting-the-sshd-backdoor-in-xz-utils
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-3094
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/04/01
tags:
  - attack.t1574.006
  - attack.t1554
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sshd'
      - '/systemd'
  selection_lib:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/liblzma.so.5.6.0'
      - '/liblzma.so.5.6.1'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_lib
falsepositives:
  - Security research / IR lab hosts intentionally running the backdoored library
  - Snapshot of an older filesystem mounted for forensic review
level: critical
3742.spl: | tstats summariesonly=t count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path, values(Filesystem.action) as action from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="liblzma.so.5.6.0" OR Filesystem.file_name="liblzma.so.5.6.1") AND (Filesystem.process_name="sshd" OR Filesystem.process_name="systemd" OR Filesystem.process_name="systemd-cryptsetup") by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.process_id, Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
3742.datadog: source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@process.name:sshd OR @process.executable.path:*/sshd OR @process.name:systemd) ("liblzma.so.5.6.0" OR "liblzma.so.5.6.1")

// Article-specific bespoke detection — GitHub “besieged” by malware repositories and repo confusion: Why you'll be ok
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("index.js", "node.js"))

| order by Timestamp desc

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("index.js", "node.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

3749.sigma:
title: Jinja2 xmlattr Filter XSS Exploitation Attempt (CVE-2024-22195)
id: 4b8c9a3e-1f2d-4e5b-8c7a-9d6e0f1b2c3d
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP requests containing the xmlattr-filter attribute-injection pattern (a space followed by an HTML event handler or src attribute) characteristic of CVE-2024-22195 exploitation against Jinja2 < 3.1.3.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/jinja2-xss-vulnerability/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-22195
  - https://github.com/pallets/jinja/security/advisories/GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/01/18
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
  - cve.2024.22195
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_handler:
    cs-uri-query|re|i: '\s(onerror|onload|onclick|onmouseover|onfocus|onsubmit|onmouseout)\s*='
  selection_src_chain:
    cs-uri-query|re|i: '\ssrc\s*=\s*\S+\s+on\w+\s*='
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Pen-testing scanners (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Nikto) replaying XSS payloads
  - Internal QA / red-team exercises
  - CMS admin endpoints that legitimately accept event-handler-bearing HTML
level: high
3749.spl:
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*onerror=*" OR Web.url="*onload=*" OR Web.url="*onclick=*" OR Web.url="*onmouseover=*" OR Web.url="*onfocus=*" OR Web.url="*onsubmit=*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method Web.status Web.user_agent _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval decoded_url=urldecode(url)
| regex decoded_url="(?i)\s+(?:onerror|onload|onclick|onmouseover|onfocus|onsubmit|onmouseout)\s*="
| eval cve="CVE-2024-22195", signature="Jinja2 xmlattr XSS attempt"
| table _time src dest url decoded_url http_method status user_agent signature cve
